name: Tomb Raider Game of the Year

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz feels smooth and is easy for the Deck to sustain at high settings with TressFX off. Light FSR upscaling from 1152x720 keeps image quality high while giving the GPU headroom.

profiles.Summary: Tomb Raider (2013) is a well-optimized older title that runs excellently on the Steam Deck, comfortably exceeding 60 fps at native resolution with medium-to-high settings. Its low PC requirements relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU mean battery-friendly play is very achievable.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2013 PC requirements (well below the Deck's capability), its Platinum ProtonDB tier, and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU. On your first run, check the frame rate in a dense jungle or combat area — if MaxPerformance dips, disable Ambient Occlusion or drop to the Optimal profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: TDP and GPU clock are aggressively limited to maximise battery; FSR upscaling from 960x600 keeps the image acceptable. TressFX and tessellation are disabled as they are the biggest GPU cost items in this title.

KnownIssues: TressFX hair simulation (Lara's hair) can cause noticeable GPU performance drops; disabling it is recommended for stable frame rates.
Some users report occasional stutters during cutscene transitions under Proton.
The game's launcher may appear on first launch; selecting 'Play' and configuring graphics from within the game is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU handles this 2013 title at native 1280x800 Ultra settings with ease; TressFX remains off as it can cause dips below 50 fps even here. Expect near-locked 60 fps in most areas with occasional dips in dense foliage or large open areas.

Optimal.Notes: This profile delivers a great-looking, smooth 60 fps experience. TressFX is kept off and tessellation disabled to preserve the headroom needed to hold the cap in dense scenes.

profiles.Summary: Tomb Raider (2013) is a relatively lightweight DirectX 11 title that runs excellently on the Steam Deck via Proton, well within the hardware's capabilities given its modest PC requirements. Expect smooth, stable frame rates at medium-to-high settings with plenty of headroom for battery savings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest 2013 PC requirements (GTX 480 recommended, well below Deck GPU class) and the platinum ProtonDB tier. On first run, confirm the in-game resolution stuck and check frame rate in the Geothermal Caverns area — the most GPU-heavy section — then adjust TDP or settings accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a 6 W TDP cap keeps the Deck very cool and quiet. TressFX is disabled as it is the single biggest GPU cost in this game.

KnownIssues: TressFX hair simulation (AMD's hair physics) can cause noticeable GPU overhead — disabling it is recommended on Deck.
The game's launcher may occasionally appear on first run; set graphics options before closing it.
Some users report the game defaults to a lower resolution on first launch — verify in-game resolution settings after starting.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with Ultra settings the Deck GPU has ample headroom for this 2013 title; TressFX is still left off as it can cause frame spikes even at max settings. Enable it only if you want to test — it may cost 10-15 fps.
